column3: fact
Mammals are characterized by milk-producing mammary glands, neocortex, fur/hair, and three middle ear bones
About 6,400 described species; grouped into 27 orders
Mammal species identified in 2006
IUCN Global Mammal Assessment counted in 2008
Recognized mammal species in 2018, including 96 recently extinct
Mammals originated from cynodonts during the Late Triassic to Early Jurassic
Mammals have been dominant terrestrial animal group from about 66 million years ago to present
Smallest mammal: bumblebee bat
Largest mammal: blue whale
Shortest listed lifespan: shrew
Longest listed lifespan: bowhead whale
All modern mammals give birth to live young except five monotreme species, which lay eggs
Most species-rich group is viviparous placental mammals
No classification system is universally accepted
Most mammals, including the six most species-rich orders, belong to the placental group
Three major placental lineages: Afrotheria, Xenarthra, Boreoeutheria
Estimated divergence times among three placental groups: 105-120 million years ago
Mammalian heart has four chambers
Hair is a definitive characteristic of mammals
Bats are the only mammals that can truly fly
Eusocial behavior demonstrated in naked mole-rat and Damaraland mole-rat
Livestock make up 62% of world mammal biomass; humans 34%; wild mammals 4%
Wild mammal biomass declined by 82% since beginning of human civilization
Decline and extinction of many mammals primarily driven by human poaching and habitat destruction/deforestation
